def: to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume)

occurrences.text: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.
And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.
For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
